description: Job Description – Data Analyst / MIS Executive – Sweet Retail & ProductionJob  Description – Data Analyst / MIS Executive  **Industry:** Sweet & Food Retail / Manufacturing  **Department:** MIS / Operations / Production Analytics  **Experience:** 4–8 Years   **Location:** Plot No 33 Mega Food Park Village Ladhowal Ludhiana  **Reporting To:** Management / Operations Head  Job Summary  We are looking for a highly skilled **Data Analyst / MIS Executive** to manage and analyze business data for **8 retail outlets and the central production unit** of a sweet manufacturing and retail business.  The candidate will be responsible for maintaining outlet-wise and production-wise databases, preparing **daily sales and wastage reports, variance reports, production reports, stock analysis, reconciliation reports, and management dashboards**.  The ideal candidate must have **excellent Advanced Excel skills** and the ability to convert large volumes of operational data into accurate reports and actionable business insights.  Key Responsibilities   1. Outlet-Wise Data Management  * Manage and maintain databases for **8 retail outlets**. * Maintain daily outlet-wise sales, stock, wastage, transfer, return, and other operational data. * Consolidate data from all outlets into centralized MIS reports. * Monitor data accuracy and identify missing, incorrect, or duplicate entries. * Maintain SKU/item-wise, category-wise, and outlet-wise databases. * Track daily, weekly, and monthly performance of each outlet.  .2. Daily Sales Analysis  * Prepare **daily outlet-wise sales reports**. * Analyze sales by outlet, product, category, SKU, quantity, and value. * Compare **actual sales vs. target/budget**. * Identify high-performing and low-performing outlets and products. * Prepare daily sales summaries for management. * Analyze sales trends and identify unusual variations.  . 3.Variance Analysis  * Prepare daily and monthly **variance reports**. * Analyze differences between: * Production vs. sales * Opening stock vs. closing stock * System stock vs. physical stock * Standard quantity vs. actual consumption * Expected wastage vs. actual wastage * Production quantity vs. dispatch quantity * Sales target vs. actual sales * Investigate significant variances and identify possible reasons. * Highlight major exceptions requiring management attention.  4. Production Unit Data Management  * Maintain daily production data for the central **sweet production unit**. * Track product-wise production quantities. * Analyze production against sales and outlet requirements. * Maintain production planning and dispatch data. * Track raw material consumption against production. * Analyze production efficiency and yield. * Monitor production wastage and process losses. * Prepare production vs. requirement reports. * Coordinate with the production team to ensure accurate data recording.  5. Stock & Inventory Analysis  * Maintain outlet-wise and production-unit stock databases. * Prepare stock movement reports. * Monitor opening stock, purchases/production, transfers, sales, wastage, returns, and closing stock. * Reconcile physical stock with system/database records. * Identify stock discrepancies and unusual movements. * Prepare slow-moving and fast-moving product reports. * Monitor stock availability across all outlets.  6. Advanced Excel & Dashboard Development  The candidate must have **excellent hands-on knowledge of Advanced Excel** and should be capable of independently developing:  * Advanced Excel dashboards * Pivot Tables and Pivot Charts * XLOOKUP / VLOOKUP * INDEX-MATCH * SUMIFS / COUNTIFS * IF / IFS / IFERROR * Dynamic formulas * Conditional Formatting * Data Validation * Slicers and Timelines * Power Query * Data consolidation * Automated MIS reports * Variance analysis models * Outlet performance dashboards * Production and wastage dashboards  7. Management Reporting  Prepare regular reports including:  * Daily Sales Report * Outlet-Wise Sales Report * Product-Wise Sales Report * Daily Wastage Report * Wastage % Report * Sales Variance Report * Production Report * Production vs. Sales Report * Stock Reconciliation Report * Outlet Stock Report * Transfer/Dispatch Report * Production Yield Report * Raw Material Consumption Report * Outlet Performance Report * Monthly MIS Report * Management Dashboard * Exception/Deviation Report  For example:  * Which outlet has the highest wastage? * Which products have abnormal wastage? * Which outlet has declining sales? * Which products are over-produced or under-produced? * Where is the highest stock variance? * Which products are fast-moving or slow-moving? * What is the production requirement based on sales trends? * Which outlet has the highest sales growth? * Where are stock or quantity mismatches occurring? * What are the major daily/monthly deviations? * What operational areas require management attention?  **Mandatory:**  * Advanced MS Excel * Data analysis * MIS reporting * Large database management * Pivot Tables * Advanced Excel formulas * Power Query * Dashboard development * Data reconciliation * Variance analysis  **Preferred:**  * Power BI * ERP/POS software experience * Retail/FMCG/Food/Sweet manufacturing data experience  Candidate Profile  The ideal candidate should:  * Have excellent numerical and analytical ability. * Be extremely strong in **Advanced Excel**. * Be comfortable handling large amounts of daily data. * Have strong attention to detail and data accuracy. * Understand sales, inventory, production, wastage, and variance concepts. * Be able to identify errors and unusual business patterns. * Be capable of independently preparing management reports. * Have good communication skills to coordinate with outlet and production teams. * Be proactive in identifying problems rather than simply preparing reports.  **Qualification**  * Bachelor's of Commerce / Master's of Business administration. * Candidates with relevant professional experience and exceptional Excel skills may also be considered.  **Experience**  * **4 to 8years of relevant experience** in Data Analysis, MIS, Reporting, Business Analysis, or a similar role. * Candidates should have demonstrated experience working extensively with **Advanced Excel and large datasets**.  **Salary & Benefits**  PF/ESI   Meal provided   Pick&drop facility   25% Bonus and 8 to 10% Increment Yearly   9 hours shift with monthly 4 offs.  Pay: ₹25,000.00 - ₹30,000.00 per month  Work Location: In person

description: **Role: Full Stack Developer / SDE**   **Experience: 3-6 years**   **Location: Indore**   **Type: Full time**  **About the role:**   We are keeping this as one role rather than two because most of our work cuts vertically. A change to how a run reports its state touches the runtime, the API contract and three screens. Splitting that across two people at our size produces handoffs, not speed.  The AI layer is only as trustworthy as the plumbing under it and only as usable as the surface over it. This role owns both.  **What you will own:**   **Backend and platform**  * FastAPI services across the Control and Agent Runtime planes. * The agent runtime harness — the generic stateless worker that loads a kit and becomes that agent for the length of one run. * Deterministic decision engines. These are pure, testable, model-free code and they are the heart of the product. * Authorisation, capability tokens and the audit path. Multi-tenancy enforced structurally rather than by convention. * Durable orchestration: retries, timers, compensation, resumption after restart. * Integration surfaces — connectors to operator systems, wrapped as tools with controlled egress. * PostgreSQL schema design, query performance and row-level isolation.  **Frontend and console**  * The React, Vite and TypeScript console. * Data-dense views: run pipelines, verdict and evidence detail, causal chain read-outs, audit views. * Real-time surfaces — server-sent event streams, live run state, partial results arriving out of order. * The copilot surface: chat, streaming responses, and a page context bus where components register structured context rather than raw state. * Geospatial and time-series visualisation. * A shared component library, built with the designer rather than after them. * Accessibility, performance and honest behaviour under bad networks and large datasets.  **Across both**  * Test coverage and performance for every path you own. * API contracts you would be happy to consume yourself — you are usually the one consuming them. * Following a bug across the boundary rather than filing it at the boundary.  **What you need**   **Backend**  * Strong Python. FastAPI, Flask or Django in production. * API design, authentication and authorisation patterns, and the discipline to version a contract properly. * PostgreSQL at depth — schema design, indexing, query performance, row-level isolation. * Async work, queues and background processing.  **Frontend**  * Strong React and TypeScript. Modern hooks, state management, composition patterns. * You have built data-dense interfaces — dashboards, operational tools, anything with too much information and not enough space. Not just marketing pages or basic CRUD. * Real-time or streaming UI: websockets, server-sent events, or equivalent. Partial and out-of-order data does not frighten you. * Charting and visualisation — Recharts, D3 or similar. * Design sense. You are often the last person between a design and the user, and you will be asked what you would change.  **Everything else**  * You write tests without being asked and can explain what each one protects. * Docker and Git. Comfortable in a Linux environment. * You use AI dev tooling heavily — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or similar — and review its output critically. We do not count tokens; we do expect you to own whatever comes back out. * You can hold a problem across the whole stack rather than handing it over at the boundary. * You explain your work clearly to engineers and to non-engineers. Writing is part of the job. description: **Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer**  TicketGateway Inc. | Full-time, permanent | On-site in Nagpur, Maharashtra  Salary: ₹80,000–1,00,000 per month  Reports to: Head of Engineering  ON-SITE ROLE — NAGPUR  Regular in-person work from our Nagpur office is a requirement for this position. Please apply only if you can work on-site in Nagpur, or relocate before joining. This is not a remote role.  ABOUT TICKETGATEWAY  TicketGateway (ticketgateway.com) is a Toronto-based, founder-led event ticketing platform serving live events across Canada, the US and the Caribbean. Our software supports ticket purchases, organizer tools, payments, ticket inventory and event scanning, including TG LiveScan. Correct transactions and dependable event-day operations matter as much as shipping new features.  THE ROLE  We are looking for a hands-on senior engineer with strong backend judgment who can own a feature or production problem from investigation through implementation, testing, deployment and follow-up. You will work with our Head of Engineering and existing team, review code, help other developers and explain technical trade-offs clearly.  Our current platform uses PHP and MySQL/MariaDB. We are also evaluating a substantial platform rebuild that may involve an external development partner. The rebuild and its technology stack are not yet committed. You will help assess options, work effectively on the existing platform and, if we proceed, review the partner’s work and help our internal team take ownership of the delivered system. This role includes ongoing maintenance and modernization, not only new development.  FEATURE IMPLEMENTATION  * Turn business and user needs into clear requirements, acceptance criteria and a practical technical approach. Discuss trade-offs with product and engineering colleagues before building.  * Implement features end-to-end: database changes, backend logic, APIs, frontend interfaces and third-party integrations. Break larger projects into useful releases and communicate estimates, dependencies and risks.  * Test normal flows, edge cases and failure scenarios; work with QA and stakeholders to validate behavior before release.  * Deploy features safely, document how they work, monitor adoption, errors and performance after launch, and iterate from user feedback and measurable results.  * Potential projects include organizer dashboards, checkout improvements, event-management tools, reporting and scanning workflows; priorities will be agreed with the team.  PLATFORM RELIABILITY AND TEAMWORK  * Build and maintain backend services, APIs and full-stack features for checkout, orders, ticket inventory and organizer workflows.  * Protect transaction correctness: handle concurrent purchases, expiring reservations, duplicate or delayed payment notifications, refunds and reconciliation without overselling or issuing duplicate tickets.  * Improve SQL queries, indexes and data models; use transactions, background jobs and caching appropriately.  * Diagnose production issues using logs and monitoring, address root causes and add meaningful regression coverage.  * Deliver maintainable code with automated tests, code review, clear deployment steps and rollback plans. Improve access controls, secrets handling and protection of customer data.  * Support reliable integrations with payment providers, email/SMS services, scanning applications and partner systems.  * Coordinate with product and engineering colleagues, break down work, communicate risks early and mentor developers through practical reviews.  POSSIBLE REBUILD AND CONTRACTOR COLLABORATION  If a rebuild proceeds, you will work with the Head of Engineering to:  * Document existing business rules and critical flows before replacing them, including orders, payments, refunds, organizer reporting and ticket validation.  * Compare proposed technologies and architecture against maintainability, delivery risk, operating costs and the internal team’s capabilities.  * Review contractor designs, code and milestones against agreed acceptance criteria; raise concerns with evidence and propose fixes.  * Plan and validate data migration, integration compatibility, performance testing, staged rollout and rollback. Check migrated orders and financial records against the source system.  * Help ensure TicketGateway has company-controlled repositories and infrastructure, repeatable deployments, useful documentation and a practical handover so the internal team can operate and extend the platform.  AI FEATURES AND DEVELOPMENT  You will help identify, design and implement useful AI-powered features for TicketGateway, as well as use AI to improve engineering delivery.  * Work with product and business teams to identify problems where AI can create measurable value, define success criteria and decide when a conventional solution is more appropriate.  * Build prototypes and take approved ideas into production, including model API integrations, relevant data retrieval, application interfaces and workflow automation. Possible applications include organizer support, event-content assistance, event discovery and internal operations; these are examples, not a committed roadmap.  * Connect AI features to authorized business data and tools with appropriate permissions, output validation and human review for consequential actions.  * Create evaluation examples and test output quality, failure cases and misuse. Monitor response time, usage cost and reliability; implement fallbacks and improve the feature using feedback.  We want evidence of practical AI experience:  * Use AI coding assistants for development, debugging, refactoring or test creation, while personally reviewing the code and verifying its behavior.  * Show at least one working AI-powered feature or internal automation you helped build using a model API or equivalent integration. Explain your contribution, how you assessed output quality and how failures were handled.  * Understand basic AI integration concerns: sensitive data, permissions, prompt injection, structured outputs, latency, cost and fallback behavior. Keep payment and ticketing decisions behind validated application rules and appropriate approvals.  You do not need to train models or be a machine-learning researcher. We value working software and sound judgment over a list of AI tool names.  WHAT YOU BRING  * A track record of independently delivering and supporting production web applications. Typically 5+ years of relevant experience, or equivalent evidence of senior-level responsibility.  * Strong backend engineering in PHP, TypeScript/Node.js or another established web stack, plus the ability and willingness to read, debug and safely modify our existing PHP application. Prior production PHP experience is strongly preferred; a PHP-only career is not required.  * Strong SQL and relational database skills, including schema design, query optimization, transactions and data integrity.  * Experience with JavaScript/TypeScript and a modern frontend framework; React is preferred.  * Experience integrating transaction-heavy systems, such as payments, e-commerce, bookings or ticketing, with a clear understanding of retries, concurrency and failure cases.  * Practical skills in Git, code review, automated testing, deployment pipelines, production monitoring and secure API design.  * Evidence of AI-assisted development and a working AI integration or automation.  * Clear communication, ownership of deadlines and quality, and the judgment to ask for help before a small risk becomes a production incident.  * Ability to work on-site in Nagpur.  HELPFUL EXPERIENCE  * CodeIgniter or Laravel; production TypeScript/Node.js services.  * Legacy modernization, data migrations or taking over software built by an agency or contractor.  * Cloud hosting, background job systems, Redis, load testing or event scanning/offline synchronization.  * Reviewing technical designs and helping a small engineering team improve its delivery practices.  FIRST 90 DAYS  Learn the existing architecture and critical business flows, ship a tested improvement, and establish a clear view of technical risks. Improve an agreed reliability or delivery issue, demonstrate effective use of AI with verified results, and contribute a practical modernization assessment. Rebuild commitments and delivery milestones will be agreed after discovery.  COMPENSATION AND DETAILS  * Salary: ₹80,000–1,00,000 per month, depending on relevant experience.  * Type: Full-time, permanent.  * Location: On-site in Nagpur, Maharashtra.  * Reports to: Head of Engineering.  HOW TO APPLY  Apply through Indeed with your resume. Email a GitHub or portfolio link, or a short description of relevant work you can discuss, to naveen@ticketgateway.com with the subject “Senior Software Engineer — [Your Name]”. Public code is helpful but not required; please do not share confidential employer or client material.  Include a brief example of a production system or difficult incident you owned, and an AI-assisted development workflow or AI integration you built. Explain what you personally did, how you verified correctness and what you learned. Confirm whether you are already in Nagpur or when you could relocate and begin working on-site. description: **The Role: Cloud & DevSecOps Engineer**  Day to day, that means designing and running our infrastructure across Google Cloud Platform and AWS, owning our GitLab CI/CD pipelines, and implementing the security controls that protect PHI and financial data.  This role has a deliberate growth path. You will start as the hands-on engineer who builds and secures the platform. Over your first year, you will work alongside the team lead and an external compliance specialist. During that time you will take on increasing ownership of our HIPAA program and SOC 2 Type II attestation, moving from implementing controls to designing and leading them. The goal is that you become our security and compliance lead. We will fund necessary training to get you there.  If you want your infrastructure and security decisions to actually matter, and you want a path from senior engineer to program owner, this is that role.  **What You'll Do**  ***Cloud Architecture: GCP and AWS***  * Design, deploy, and operate our SaaS infrastructure across GCP and AWS using HIPAA-aligned reference architectures. * Make sure every workload touching PHI runs only on HIPAA-eligible services. Business Associate Agreements must be signed for each cloud account and project before any PHI lands. * Implement network segmentation and VPC design, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS key management, and least-privilege IAM across both clouds. * Build everything as infrastructure-as-code with Terraform. Environments should be reproducible, reviewable, and auditable.  ***DevOps and GitLab CI/CD***  * Own and improve our GitLab CI/CD pipelines end to end: build, test, scan, deploy. * Integrate security scanning into the pipeline (SAST, dependency and SCA scanning, container and IaC scanning) without turning delivery into a crawl. * Manage secrets, artifacts, and release processes securely. Keep PHI out of logs, caches, and lower environments. * Support the development team. Good pipelines make other engineers faster, not slower.  ***Security Engineering***  * Implement and maintain technical safeguards: phishing-resistant MFA, centralized audit logging, monitoring and alerting, vulnerability management, and incident response. * Enforce bastion or VDI-only production access with no local download of PHI, backed by DLP and egress controls. * Keep production access minimal and regularly reviewed. Use de-identified or synthetic data in development and test environments. * Respond to security events and lead post-incident reviews.  ***Compliance: HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II, Plaid***  *Starting out, you implement and evidence. Over time, you design and lead.*  * Implement the technical controls behind our HIPAA Security Rule safeguards and SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, then take ownership of the program as you grow into the role. * Operate our compliance automation platform (Vanta, Drata, or Secureframe): keep evidence collection running, monitor for control drift, close gaps. * Own the security side of our Plaid integration. That means TLS 1.2+ and mTLS where required, encrypted secrets, least-privilege access to financial data, and monitoring for unauthorized access. You will also support Plaid's production access review and security questionnaire. Handling consumer financial data carries GLBA and FTC Safeguards Rule obligations, and you will help us meet them. * Support penetration tests and audits: help scope them, coordinate with the testers and auditor, and drive remediation. * Over time, you will lead the HIPAA risk analysis, own control design, select and manage the external auditor, and carry us through the SOC 2 Type II observation period.  **What You Need**  * 3+ years in cloud engineering, DevOps, or DevSecOps. * Hands-on production experience on both GCP and AWS. Not one cloud plus a certification in the other: real production work in both. * Strong GitLab CI/CD experience, or equivalent CI/CD depth and the ability to move to GitLab quickly. * Terraform and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes). * Practical security engineering: IAM and least privilege, encryption, secrets management, network security, logging and monitoring. * Working exposure to HIPAA or SOC 2 in practice. You should be able to explain what a control is and how you'd evidence it. * The judgment to handle PHI responsibly and work inside strict access controls. * Clear written and spoken English. You will document data flows, controls, and decisions that auditors and customers read.  **Nice to Have**  * Prior work at a healthcare, fintech, or other regulated SaaS company handling sensitive data. * Hands-on experience with a compliance automation platform (Vanta, Drata, Secureframe, Sprinto). * Experience integrating a financial data provider such as Plaid, and awareness of GLBA / FTC Safeguards Rule obligations. * Any of these certifications: AWS Solutions Architect Professional, AWS Security Specialty, Google Professional Cloud Architect, Google Professional Cloud Security Engineer, CISSP, CCSP, CISM, HITRUST CCSFP. * Experience working directly with external auditors or remediating penetration test findings.  **How To Apply:** Share your CV on careers@dronatechlabs.com  Pay: ₹80,000.00 - ₹100,000.00 per month  Benefits:  * Flexible schedule  Work Location: In person

We would rather be argued with than agreed with, and we would rather be remembered than be safe.  **ABOUT US** ------------  Our client is a new venture by a leading Indian consumer brand builder. We are in the business of building tasteful brands across categories and geographies. That could mean 0 to 1, 1 to 10, or 10 to 1000. Six months in, we are about 25 people, each one here to do the best work of our lives.  The founder did not build a leading consumer brand by making good products. He built it by understanding what a generation of Indians wanted to feel about themselves, and then making that buyable. We are doing that again, across more categories, for more kinds of Indians, from scratch.  **WHY WE ARE HIRING** ---------------------  We need someone to run one of our brands. The brand is deeply rooted in South India. Its culture, its rituals, its everyday habits. The category it walks into has spent decades selling the past. Heritage, nostalgia, sepia, hand-pounded, home-style, authentic since 19-whatever. Almost none of its language speaks to how people actually live and shop right now.  We are building a culture-first brand. A regional representation of taste, in the present tense, with a point of view. Rooted enough to carry real authority, current enough to sit in a 24-year-old’s cart without explaining itself.  There will be a creative lead on this brand who owns what it looks like and sounds like. You own how to make the brand work. The plan, the portfolio, the money, the partners, the calendar, the shelf.  We are looking for someone who already understands this market or can build a plan around it and execute end-to-end. More on the category and the brand once we are talking properly.  **WHAT YOU WILL OWN** ---------------------  * The brand plan. What we launch, when, for whom, with what money. Annual on paper, quarterly in practice, and rewritten the moment the market says something different. * The consumer. Who buys, who almost buys, and what makes someone switch after twenty years of buying the same thing. Some of that comes from data. Most of it comes from reginal learning. * The portfolio. Pack sizes, price points, the SKU ladder, what launches and what gets killed. You bring the market back to product and supply chain as a point of view, not as a list of requests. * Go to market. Launch sequence, city by city and channel by channel. Where we start, where we deliberately do not, and what has to be true before we widen. * Channels. Quick commerce, marketplaces, modern trade, general trade, D2C. Listings, content, ratings, share of search, the merchandising calendar. A lot of this is unglamorous and it still decides the year. * Media and budget. Where the money goes, what came back, what gets cut. You will defend a spend line, and you will also be the one to kill your own. * The numbers. Awareness, trial, repeat, velocity per store, ROAS, share of search. You own the dashboard and you report it honestly, including the months it looks bad. * Briefs. Written so a creative team can act on them. One problem, one real constraint, one thing to say. Then you get out of the way and let them make it better than the brief. * Activations, brand partnerships, regional calendars. In this category, tasting beats telling, and you plan for that from day one. * The cross-functional mess. Founders, supply chain, sales, growth, product. A launch slips because packaging is stuck at a printer, and you are the person who knows that before anyone tells you.  **CULTURAL FLUENCY, WHAT WE ACTUALLY MEAN** -------------------------------------------  * You truly believe the representation of South India by brands so far has been extremely surface level, and you can name the specific work that proves your point. * You understand that the southern states are four different markets, not one segment. Different retail, different price expectations, different reasons to pick something up. * You know which festivals move sales and which only move greetings. * You are fluent in at least one South Indian language. Fluent enough to stand in a shop, ask a real question and follow the answer the shopkeeper gives the customer next to you. * You can read a line of regional copy and tell whether it sounds like a person or like it went through Google Translate. And you push back when it is the latter.  **THIS IS FOR YOU IF** ----------------------  A tidy deck and a media plan do not tell us much. We want someone with a point of view about this market and the numbers to argue it with. And is a go getter who runs the brand.  ### **Must have**  * Three or more years in brand or marketing, with real ownership. A brand, a category or a launch that was actually yours. * South Indian cultural fluency, exactly as described above. * Comfort with numbers. You can build a plan, defend it line by line, and spot the month where it quietly stops making sense. * Judgment on spend. Deciding what not to fund is the harder half of the job. * You can write a brief a creative person actually wants to work on. * Execution across levels. A pricing conversation at 11am, fixing a listing title or chasing a vendor at 8pm. * Comfort with ambiguity. No playbook, and no category norms we intend to inherit. * You can think without AI. Use the tools to move faster, never to think for you.  ### **Strongly preferred**  * Food or FMCG background. You know packaging is the biggest media buy, that sampling converts, and roughly what FSSAI will and will not let you print on a pack. * A 0 to 1 launch. You have taken something from nothing to on-shelf, and you remember what broke. * Quick commerce and marketplace depth. Listings, ads, assortment, share of search. * Time inside a large FMCG system and time inside a startup. One taught you rigour, the other taught you speed. * Real experience in southern markets. Distributors, trade, regional media, local creators. * Experience managing agencies, vendors and a small team.  ### **And the quirks**  * You know the difference between a brand that is famous and a brand that is bought, and you can name one of each. * You read the back of packs in other people’s trolleys. * There is a regional brand you admire that never ran a national campaign, and you know exactly why it worked. * You hold strong opinions about a shelf you had nothing to do with.  **WHY JOIN** ------------  Full ownership of a brand at a house of brands, from day zero. Direct access to one of the sharpest consumer brand builders in India. And the chance to build something rooted in a culture that most national brands still market to badly.

title: Product Manager
description: 3-5  Europa Bangalore  Full-Time  **About the role**  You have personally shipped a consumer financial product to real users — and you can name the line of code, the policy clause, or the CS conversation that broke things and what you did about it. Not "led a team that shipped." Not "owned the roadmap." You wrote the spec, you sat in CS calls, you queried the data yourself, you watched the dashboards on launch night.      That is the qualifying condition for this role. Everything else in this document is for people who pass that bar. If you do not pass it, no amount of brand-name PMs on your resume, MBA pedigree, or strategy deck experience makes up for it. We will know within ten minutes of an interview. Save us both the time.  If you do pass it, this is the role you have been waiting for.      **The bet**  Every fintech in India is shipping the same feature set: savings, cards, investments, wrap-around banking. We are betting that the company that ships them with the most opinionated taste — fewer screens, fewer settings, fewer apologies — owns the next decade of consumer finance in India. That bet runs through every PM here.      You will own a consumer-facing surface end to end. Roadmap, specs, design partnership, engineering partnership, CS feedback loops, compliance review, launch operation, post-launch retention. You will not have a strategy team. You will not have a research team. You will not have a launch ops team. You will be all of those things.      **The team you'll work with — small, young, fast, default-AI**  Most of the people you will work with are in their twenties or early thirties. The defaults are "build it yourself, ship it tonight, fix it tomorrow." Meetings are short. Documents are shorter.  The right hire treats this as a feature, not a compromise. You will be one PM among a handful, owning a meaningful surface. You will move at the engineering team's pace, not slower. You will earn their respect by writing the SQL alongside them, not by holding alignment reviews.      If you have spent the last three years building scaffolding around yourself — PgM partners, ops partners, strategy partners, BI partners — you will struggle here. If the thought of doing your own data pull at 11pm to settle a launch question makes you happy, read on.      **What makes this different from the same title anywhere else**  The surface is the company, not a screen. Most PM roles at this band own a flow. You will own a value-prop. The decision on whether we launch a feature on a regulated entity vs. a PPI rail goes through you.      You will use AI as a first-class teammate, not as a feature to add. The spec you write, the CS analysis you do, the user research you run, the launch comms you draft — they all use models. You won't get points for "leveraging AI." You will lose points for not.      It is regulated infrastructure, and that is a feature. Two RBI-licensed entities sit underneath the surface. Most of your launches will pass through a compliance review you will sit in. The moat that comes with doing it right is real.      You will work next to peers who match your bar. The Director of Product (AI), the Director of Engineering (AI), and the founding PMs all hire to this same filter.      **What you'll own**  The end-to-end PRD. Customer problem statement, the chosen segment, the named alternative we will not build, the metric we will move, the kill criteria. Written in markdown, not Confluence. No longer than two pages.      The launch decision. Whether we ship, whether we delay, whether we kill. You will own the data pull that supports the call. You will own the conversation with the founder when the data disagrees with the plan.      The CS feedback loop. You will read CS tickets for your surface daily. You will sit on a CS call weekly. You will know the top three reasons users complain about your feature within a week of launch. You will turn at least one of them into a shipped fix within two weeks.      The compliance partnership. You will sit in the compliance review for every regulated decision. You will know what RBI, NBFC, PPI, and DPDP each constrain and where they intersect. You will not delegate this to a compliance partner who walks into the meeting cold.      The taste call. You will be the final arbiter of one specific screen, one specific copy line, one specific entry point. When engineering disagrees, you will hold it. When design disagrees, you will hold it. When you are wrong, you will admit it within a week and ship the fix.      **What we're looking for, beyond the qualifying filter**  Operator instincts. When something is wrong with a launch, you read the events, write the SQL, talk to the user, file the bug. You do not "ask the team to look into it."  Range across products. You will not own one surface for years. As Jupiter moves, your remit will too — savings one quarter, cards the next, payments the one after. If you need 18 months to "really understand a domain" before you can contribute, this is not a match. You are at home in week three on a new product because you read the events, talked to ten users, and shipped a small fix. This one is non-negotiable.      Fintech experience is a tailwind, not a requirement. If you have shipped consumer products in another domain — health, ed-tech, gaming, commerce — the qualifying filter and the operator instincts matter more than the category. The compliance literacy is teachable in the first 90 days; the operator instincts are not.      Spec discipline. Your specs are short, specific, and falsifiable. You name the metric, the threshold, and the kill criteria upfront. You do not write "drive engagement." Default-AI fluency. You can write a Cursor or Claude agent prompt that pulls a product question from the team Slack and answers it from the metrics warehouse. You have done this. You can show us.      Cost and latency taste. You know how much an LLM call costs and how long it takes. You know which decisions belong to a model and which belong to a rule. You have killed a feature for being too slow, and you can tell us which one.  Comfort with a small, fast team. You see "the team is small" as freedom, not as understaffing. You ask "can an agent do this" before you ask "who can we hire to do this."      **What you won't do**  Run quarterly OKR ceremonies. Write 20-page strategy decks no one reads. Outsource customer research to a vendor. Hand off launches to a launch operations team. Build scaffolding to feel senior. Spend any time defending why product matters at Jupiter. The bet is made.      **What success looks like at six months**  You own your surface end to end. Leadership is no longer in the launch decision Slack thread. The top three CS complaints from your launches are down meaningfully against a day-one baseline. You have shipped at least one decision that the rest of the org has copied. The team that was small and fast when you joined is still small and fast.      **The basics**  Experience: 3 to 5 years. We are looking for PMs early in the build-it-yourself phase of their career, not people who have already moved on to running rituals.      Compensation: ₹30L to ₹50L cash, plus an equity package sized to be material at exit. We pay at the top of the Indian consumer fintech market for this band. If you are exceptional, we will go higher. We will be specific about valuation, strike, vesting, and the math in the conversation.      Location: Bangalore, in person. This is not a remote role.      Reporting: Reports to the Director of Product.      **How to apply**  Send us the product you shipped. A link to the live feature, a screenshot of the dashboard on launch day, a screen recording of the user reaction. One paragraph on what you would change about it now and why. We will read this before we read your resume.      Required Skills  prd product manager

description: **EZHOMZ**  Luxury Residential Automation · Smart Building Integration · Delhi NCR  **We are hiring**  **Project LEAD**  Home Automation & Lighting Control  **Location- Okhla Phase 1**  **Experience- 8-10 yrs in HOME AUTOMATION**  **Reports to- CEO**  **Type-Full time, on site**  **Delhi NCR**  **Read this line first.** This role is for someone who has personally programmed automation systems — KNX, Lutron, Crestron, Control4, RTI or ELAN — and has since moved into managing projects without losing that ability. If you have coordinated automation work but never opened the programming software yourself, this is not the right role for you, and we would rather say so here than at the interview.  **About EZHOMZ**  EZHOMZ designs and delivers automation for luxury residences across Delhi NCR — KNX and DALI lighting control, curtain and comfort systems, and OKAS integration, working with brands including Ekinex, Moorgen and Blacknova. Our clients are homeowners with high expectations and architects and interior designers who hold us to their standard.  We are deliberately building EZHOMZ into a professionally managed company rather than a founder-dependent one. This seat is a central part of that: it exists so that projects run on their own momentum, with the founder consulted on decisions rather than chased for them.  **The role**  You will own three to six live residences at a time, from the point the BOQ is approved through to client sign-off and handover into service. You are the person who knows the state of every one of them without being asked, and who never lets one slip because another was loud.  This is not a coordination seat. You will size the programming work honestly, challenge an optimistic estimate, cover a programmer who is unavailable, and hold a technical position in front of an architect or an MEP consultant without escalating it. That is why the programming background matters: a manager who can open the project file is a different animal from one who can only ask about it.  **What you will actually do**  – **Own the delivery plan.** Convert the approved automation BOQ into a sequenced site plan — first fix, conduiting and back-boxes, panel space, device mounting, commissioning, scene programming, client training, handover.  – **Drive site readiness.** Work ahead of the trades so our team never mobilises to a site that is not ready. Get conduiting and back-box positions right with the electrician and the interior designer before the ceiling closes, because after that everything costs ten times more.  – **Own the programming plan.** Size the work, supervise or perform the platform programming, and validate the system yourself before it goes anywhere near the client.  – **Run the cadence.** A live schedule, a weekly progress report the client can read, a decision log, and drawing revision control. Escalations arrive with a recommendation attached, or they are not escalations.  – **Protect the commercials.** Defend the BOQ, price variations honestly, verify vendor bills, and raise commercial exposure early rather than at handover.  – **Coordinate the ecosystem.** Architect, interior designer, MEP consultant, electrician, carpenter, site engineer and vendor partners — everyone should know what is needed, by whom, by when, and what it depends on.  – **Carry the client relationship on site.** Set expectations, avoid surprises, and leave every interaction with the client more confident than before it. Never expose internal confusion.  – **Close properly.** Client training at handover, a complete documentation pack, and a clean transition into service and AMC.  **Essential — we will not compromise on these**  – **Hands-on programming on KNX (ETS) or Lutron.** You have built the topology, addressed the devices, written the scenes and commissioned on site yourself — not stood beside the person who did.  – **Working capability on at least one control platform:** Crestron, Control4, RTI or ELAN. Tell us which, and which software you used.  – **The journey: engineer, then programmer, then project ownership.** At least two years in a programming seat before you moved into managing.  – **4–10 years total experience**, with the ability to run three or more live residences concurrently.  – **Presence.** You can sit with an HNI client, an architect and an interior designer, hold the room, and write to them afterwards in a way that builds confidence.  – **Delhi NCR base**, or a genuine willingness to relocate.  **Desirable, not essential**  – DALI commissioning depth — short addressing, groups and scenes, and what has to happen when a fixture is replaced after handover.  – KNX Partner certification, or a Crestron, Control4, Lutron, RTI or ELAN dealer certification.  – Experience of luxury residential finish standards, and the disruption tolerance that comes with working in an occupied home.  – A scheduling and reporting habit you can show us, not only describe.  – Exposure to OKAS or comparable integration platforms.  **This role is probably not for you if**  – You have managed automation projects without ever programming one. You would spend the first year unable to judge the work your team is doing, and you would not enjoy it.  – You want one flagship project to pour yourself into. This seat runs several at once, and the skill is holding all of them.  – You would rather be at a desk than on site. Much of this job happens standing in a half-built room with a drawing in your hand.  **What we offer**  – **Complete residences, not fragments.** You own the project from BOQ handover to sign-off, with real decision authority inside it.  – **An engineered standard to work from.** Our BOQ logic, design standards and technical references already exist, so your time goes into delivery rather than reinvention.  – **Direct access to the founder** and a genuine say in how the delivery function is built, at a moment when it is being built.  – **Continued technical growth.** We will fund platform certification. We would rather you got better at the craft than drifted away from it.  – **Compensation:** Depends on Interview  **How to apply**  Write to **hr@ezhomz.com or DM at 9899917916** with your CV and a short note answering three things:  – Which platforms have you personally programmed, and which software did you use?  – What is the most difficult commissioning problem you have solved yourself — what went wrong, what you tried, and how it ended?  – How many projects were you running at the same time, at peak?  *We read these properly. A specific, honest answer to the second question will get you further than a long CV.*  Pay: ₹600,000.00 - ₹800,000.00 per year  Benefits:  * Cell phone reimbursement * Provident Fund  Work Location: In person

Food Department Operations  * Manage and supervise the day-to-day operations of the food department. * Ensure timely preparation and distribution of meals as per the approved menu and requirements. * Coordinate with chefs, kitchen staff, dieticians, service staff, and other departments. * Monitor food quality, portion control, taste, presentation, and service standards. * Ensure adequate manpower allocation and efficient utilization of resources. * Monitor daily production and consumption of food items.  2. Cost Control  * Monitor and control overall food production and operational costs. * Prepare and monitor food cost on a daily, weekly, and monthly basis. * Control food wastage, overproduction, spillage, and unnecessary consumption. * Monitor portion sizes and standard recipes to maintain consistent food cost. * Compare actual consumption with budgeted consumption and identify variations. * Analyze food cost variance and take corrective actions. * Identify opportunities for cost reduction without compromising food quality and safety. * Monitor labour, utility, consumable, and other operational expenses related to the food department.  3. Wastage Control  * Monitor daily food and material wastage. * Identify the reasons for wastage and implement corrective measures. * Maintain proper wastage records. * Reduce wastage through proper production planning, portion control, inventory rotation, and forecasting. * Review wastage trends periodically and report significant variations to management.  9. Staff Management  * Supervise and guide food department employees. * Prepare duty allocation and ensure adequate staffing. * Monitor staff attendance, discipline, productivity, and performance. * Provide training on food safety, hygiene, SOPs, equipment handling, and operational procedures. * Conduct regular team briefings and communicate operational requirements.  10. Documentation & Reporting  * Maintain accurate operational records and reports. * Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly reports related to: * Food cost * Inventory * Stock movement * Food wastage * Purchase and consumption * Production * Complaints * Food safety and hygiene * Manpower * Review records regularly and take corrective action for deviations. * Maintain proper documentation for audits and inspections.  11. Compliance & Audit  * Ensure compliance with organizational SOPs and applicable food safety requirements. * Support internal and external audits. * Ensure audit observations are addressed within the required timeline. * Follow up on corrective actions and maintain supporting documentation. * Ensure continuous improvement in food department operations. Restaurant, Kitchen & Bar Operations -  * Oversee restaurant, kitchen and cocktail bar operations, ensuring consistently high standards of food, beverages, service, hygiene and presentation. * Work closely with the Chef and F&B/Bar leadership on menus, seasonal offerings, cocktails and guest experience. * Monitor food and beverage costs, wastage, portion control, stock movement, inventory and overall departmental profitability. * Ensure food safety, beverage storage, responsible alcohol service and applicable compliance requirements are consistently maintained. * Regularly review restaurant and bar performance, guest feedback, covers, average spend and opportunities to improve revenue.  Private Bookings, Weddings & Special Occasions -  * Oversee private dining, group bookings, birthdays, proposals, weddings and other celebrations from planning through execution. * Coordinate requirements between clients, planners, vendors and internal departments including accommodation, F&B, kitchen, bars, security and operations. * Review packages, quotations, menus, layouts, entertainment, accommodation requirements and operational timelines. * Ensure commitments made to clients remain commercially viable and are delivered to the expected standard. description: **Operations Manager – Community Kitchen & Food Distribution**  Dream & Beauty Charitable Trust (DBCT)  Location: Delhi  Work Location: In Person  Meals Served: 10,000+ meals daily  About the Role  Dream & Beauty Charitable Trust is looking for a highly responsible, hands-on and experienced Operations Manager to manage our Delhi BBU community kitchen and food distribution operations. Inventory & Stock Management**  Monitor consumption and stock levels of food ingredients and operational supplies. Food Quality, Safety & Hygiene**  Ensure high standards of cleanliness, personal hygiene and safe food handling throughout the kitchen.  Monitor hygiene during:  \* Receiving and storage  \* Washing and preparation  \* Cooking  \* Packing  \* Loading  \* Transportation  \* Distribution  Ensure kitchen equipment, preparation areas, utensils, storage areas and food transportation containers/vehicles are maintained appropriately.  Ensure applicable organizational SOPs and food-safety requirements are followed.  **5. Staff Management & Attendance**  Supervise cooks, helpers, drivers and other support staff. Dispatch & Food Distribution**  Plan and supervise the timely loading and dispatch of prepared meals.  Coordinate vehicles, drivers, routes and distribution requirements to ensure food reaches designated locations safely and on schedule.  Maintain appropriate records of quantities dispatched and locations served.  Immediately escalate delays, vehicle breakdowns, shortages or other issues that may affect distribution.  **8. Vehicle & Fleet Coordination**  Monitor vehicles used for food distribution and ensure they remain operational and appropriately maintained. Documentation & Daily Reporting  Maintain clear and verifiable operational records.  Provide Management with regular reports covering areas such as:  \* Meals prepared and dispatched  \* Procurement and expenditure  \* Stock and consumption  \* Staff attendance  \* Staff deployment  \* Vehicle deployment  \* Operational problems  \* Wastage or discrepancies  \* Corrective actions taken  Records must be maintained accurately and made available to Management whenever required.  **10. Financial Accountability & Transparency**  This position involves responsibility for charitable resources and therefore requires a high degree of integrity and transparency.  The Manager will be expected to ensure that purchases, stock movement, consumption, manpower deployment and operational expenses are properly documented and verifiable.  Any discrepancy, wastage, unusual expenditure or operational concern must be promptly brought to Management’s attention. What This Role Requires  Candidates should apply only if they are comfortable taking end-to-end operational responsibility for a large community food program. description: JOB DESCRIPTION – QUALITY MANAGER  **Designation:** Quality Manager   **Department:** Quality Assurance / Quality Control   **Location:** Mysore, Karnataka   **Reporting To:** General Manager / Operations Head / Plant Head   **Industry:** Automotive Plastic Injection Moulding   **Nature of Business:** Manufacturing of critical insert-moulded plastic components for automobile applications, including Starter & Alternator parts   **Experience:** 8–15 years preferred in Automotive / Plastic Injection Moulding / Auto Component Industry   **Qualification:** B.E./B.Tech/Diploma in Mechanical / Polymer / Plastics / Production / Industrial Engineering or equivalent   **Preferred Knowledge:** IATF 16949, ISO 9001, APQP, PPAP, FMEA, MSA, SPC, 8D, CAPA, Control Plan, Process Audit and Customer Quality Requirements  2. JOB PURPOSE  The Quality Manager is responsible for establishing, maintaining and continuously improving the company's complete quality management system and ensuring that **100% of supplied products meet customer specifications, drawings, standards and agreed quality requirements**.  The position carries overall responsibility for:  * Incoming quality * In-process quality * Final inspection * Pre-dispatch quality * Customer complaints * Supplier quality * Process capability * Quality documentation * Corrective and preventive actions * Internal and process audits * IATF-related compliance * Quality improvement * Rejection reduction * Customer satisfaction * Quality team performance  The Quality Manager must ensure that **no defective, doubtful or non-conforming material is knowingly released to the customer**.  For critical automobile components, particular importance must be given to **visual defects, dimensional accuracy, insert positioning, moulding defects, functional requirements and traceability**, because quality failures can result in customer rejection, production-line disruption and serious downstream consequences.  3. KEY RESPONSIBILITIESA. OVERALL QUALITY MANAGEMENT  * Take complete ownership of the quality function of the factory. * Establish and maintain effective quality standards for all manufacturing processes. * Ensure that quality requirements are clearly understood and followed by Production, Stores, Maintenance, Tool Room, Purchase and other departments. * Define quality objectives and monitor achievement against targets. * Establish systems to achieve: * 100% good quality * Minimum customer complaints * Minimum internal rejection * Minimum rework * Zero dispatch of non-conforming material * Effective traceability * Compliance with customer requirements * Ensure effective implementation of documented procedures, work instructions, inspection standards and quality records. * Review quality performance on a daily, weekly and monthly basis. * Identify recurring quality problems and implement permanent corrective action rather than temporary containment.  4. INCOMING QUALITY CONTROL  The Quality Manager shall ensure that all incoming materials are controlled before being released for production.  Responsibilities include:  * Establish incoming inspection standards for raw materials, bought-out components, inserts, packaging materials and other critical items. * Ensure inspection as per specifications, drawings, standards and approved samples. * Verify material certificates wherever required. * Ensure proper identification and segregation of: * Accepted material * Rejected material * Hold material * Pending inspection material * Monitor supplier quality performance. * Coordinate with Purchase and Stores for supplier-related quality issues. * Ensure proper records for incoming inspection. * Prevent unapproved or non-conforming material from entering production.  5. IN-PROCESS QUALITY CONTROL  The Quality Manager shall ensure that quality is built into the process rather than detected only at final inspection.  Responsibilities include:  * Establish inspection frequency and inspection methods. * Ensure first-piece / first-off approval after: * Machine setup * Mould change * Material change * Process parameter change * Insert change * Tool maintenance * Verify critical process parameters. * Ensure production operators follow approved work instructions and inspection standards. * Monitor injection moulding parameters affecting product quality. * Ensure effective control of: * Short moulding * Flash * Sink marks * Weld lines * Burn marks * Flow marks * Black spots * Colour variation * Warpage * Cracks * Voids * Dimensional deviations * Insert misalignment * Insert damage * Missing inserts * Contamination * Burrs and sharp edges * Assembly-related defects * Ensure suitable control of critical-to-quality characteristics.  6. VISUAL QUALITY CONTROL  Since the company manufactures critical automobile components, the Quality Manager must establish strong visual inspection discipline.  Responsibilities include:  * Develop approved visual standards and defect samples. * Define acceptable and unacceptable visual limits. * Train inspectors and operators on visual defects. * Ensure adequate lighting and proper inspection conditions. * Establish defect photographs / visual standards at inspection stations. * Ensure inspectors understand customer-specific appearance requirements. * Prevent subjective inspection decisions by establishing clear acceptance criteria. * Periodically validate inspectors' understanding and inspection effectiveness. * Conduct layered verification of visual inspection activities.  7. FINAL INSPECTION & PRE-DISPATCH QUALITY  The Quality Manager shall ensure that only fully conforming products are dispatched.  Responsibilities include:  * Establish final inspection procedures. * Ensure inspection against: * Drawing * Customer specification * Approved sample * Control Plan * Work instruction * Packaging standard * Ensure correct quantity verification. * Ensure proper identification and traceability. * Verify batch / lot information wherever applicable. * Ensure rejected, reworked and approved materials are clearly segregated. * Verify all required inspection reports before dispatch. * Implement release authority for final product. * Ensure no material is dispatched without required quality clearance.  8. CUSTOMER COMPLAINT MANAGEMENT  The Quality Manager shall take complete ownership of customer complaints.  Responsibilities include:  * Immediately communicate customer complaints to relevant departments. * Establish containment action without delay. * Identify affected lots, production periods, machines and batches. * Stop further dispatch wherever necessary. * Investigate the actual root cause. * Use structured problem-solving methods such as: * 5 Why * Fishbone Analysis * 8D * Pareto Analysis * Why-Why Analysis * Implement permanent corrective actions. * Verify effectiveness of corrective actions. * Prepare professional customer response reports. * Maintain complete complaint history. * Monitor recurring complaints and ensure they are not repeated. * Conduct lessons-learned activities across similar products and processes.  9. CUSTOMER QUALITY REQUIREMENTS  The Quality Manager shall ensure complete understanding and implementation of customer-specific requirements.  This includes:  * Customer specifications * Customer quality standards * Special characteristics * Packaging requirements * Traceability requirements * Inspection requirements * PPAP requirements * Change-management requirements * Customer portals / reporting requirements * Customer audit requirements  The Quality Manager shall ensure that changes in customer requirements are communicated to all concerned departments and incorporated into relevant documents and processes.  10. APQP / PPAP RESPONSIBILITIES  For new products, development projects and process changes, the Quality Manager shall coordinate and ensure appropriate quality planning.  Responsibilities include:  * APQP coordination * Process Flow Diagram * PFMEA * Control Plan * Work Instructions * Inspection Standards * MSA requirements * Capability studies * PPAP documentation * Sample inspection * Dimensional reports * Material reports * Performance test reports * Process validation * Run-at-Rate support * Customer submission and approval  No new product or significant process change should be released without required quality evaluation and approval.  11. PFMEA & CONTROL PLAN MANAGEMENT  The Quality Manager shall ensure that PFMEA and Control Plans remain active working documents rather than merely audit documents.  Responsibilities include:  * Lead PFMEA reviews. * Ensure process risks are properly identified. * Link identified risks with corresponding controls. * Ensure special characteristics are identified. * Update PFMEA after: * Customer complaints * Internal rejection * Process failures * Engineering changes * Tool changes * New risks * Ensure Control Plans reflect actual shop-floor conditions. * Verify that operators are working according to the latest approved documents.  12. SPC & PROCESS CAPABILITY  The Quality Manager shall establish effective statistical monitoring for critical characteristics.  Responsibilities include:  * Identify critical and special characteristics. * Establish SPC requirements. * Monitor process capability. * Review Cp / Cpk where applicable. * Identify process trends before defects occur. * Conduct capability studies. * Ensure corrective action where process capability is inadequate. * Train quality and production personnel on basic statistical concepts.  13. MSA / GAUGE CONTROL  The Quality Manager shall ensure reliability of inspection and measurement systems.  Responsibilities include:  * Establish gauge calibration systems. * Ensure all measuring instruments are identified and traceable. * Prevent use of expired / overdue calibration instruments. * Coordinate external calibration where required. * Conduct Gauge R&R / MSA studies where applicable. * Maintain calibration records. * Ensure proper handling and storage of measuring instruments. * Evaluate suitability of inspection equipment for critical dimensions.  14. INTERNAL QUALITY AUDITS  The Quality Manager shall plan and conduct internal audits.  This includes:  * System audits * Process audits * Product audits * Layered process audits * 5S / discipline  Pay: ₹22,000.00 - ₹40,000.00 per month  Benefits:  * Health insurance  Work Location: In person

title: Sr Content Writer (Children's Books)
description: **About Kidureka**  Kidureka creates thoughtfully designed books, toys, and play experiences for children aged 2+ years. We believe children learn best when they are curious, engaged, and having fun.  We are building a team that understands children deeply and can turn ideas into products that are both meaningful and delightful to experience.  Website: www.kidureka.com  **About the Role**  We are looking for a **Senior Content Writer & Editor** with strong experience in **children’s books and children’s publishing**.  This is not a conventional content-writing role. We are looking for someone who understands that creating a children’s book is not simply about writing a good copy. It is about understanding the child, building the right narrative, structuring information appropriately, creating moments of curiosity and engagement, and working closely with the design team to bring the complete book to life.  You should be a **strong storyteller, an exceptional editor, highly attentive to detail, and deeply child-first in your thinking**.  You will work on books from idea to final execution — developing, writing, editing, refining, and collaborating with designers throughout the process.  **What You Will DoOwn content end-to-end**  Take ownership of the content of a book from the initial idea through final production.  You will be expected to:  ● Understand the objective, age group, format, and learning/play intent of each book.  ● Develop the content structure, flow, tone, and narrative.  ● Write original stories, activities, explanations, prompts, conversations, educational content, and other book formats.  ● Build on concepts and briefs provided by the team, while also bringing your own ideas and creative thinking.  ● Edit and refine content multiple times based on feedback, testing, and design requirements.  ● Ensure consistency in voice, language, facts, terminology, characters, and overall narrative across the book.  **Be an excellent storyteller**  We need someone who genuinely knows how to tell a story for a child.  You should be able to:  ● Write stories that are engaging, age-appropriate, and emotionally resonant.  ● Create strong openings, pacing, progression, and endings.  ● Make educational content feel interesting rather than instructional or textbook-like.  ● Understand how humour, curiosity, surprise, conflict, repetition, imagination, and emotion work differently for children of different ages.  ● Translate complex ideas into language that children can naturally understand.  ● Develop characters, situations, and worlds that feel relatable to children.  **Bring a child-first lens**  Everything you create should begin with the question:  **“How will a child experience this?”**  You should be able to think deeply about:  ● What a child will understand or misunderstand.  ● What will hold their attention.  ● What will make them curious enough to continue.  ● Whether the language feels natural for the intended age group.  ● Whether the content respects a child's intelligence without becoming too complex.  ● Whether a page feels engaging, overwhelming, boring, confusing, or delightful.  **Work closely with the design team**  Content and design at Kidureka are closely connected.  You will work alongside designers and illustrators throughout the book-making process to ensure the content and visual language work together.  This includes:  ● Communicating the intent behind the content clearly to designers.  ● Discussing page flow, storytelling beats, hierarchy, visual cues, and content placement.  ● Understanding how text, illustration, typography, activities, icons, and visual elements work together.  ● Reviewing designed pages and identifying content-related issues in the visual execution.  ● Suggesting where content needs to be shortened, expanded, rearranged, clarified, or visually supported.  ● Collaborating on how an idea can best be communicated to a child through a combination of words and visuals.  **You will not be responsible for making design decisions, but you must have strong visual literacy and understand how content and design come together to create the final experience.**  **Be the eye for detail**  Children’s publishing requires an extremely high level of accuracy.  You will be responsible for identifying and resolving:  ● Grammar, spelling, punctuation, and syntax errors.  ● Inconsistencies in language, terminology, names, facts, and formatting.  ● Age-inappropriate or unclear language.  ● Repetition and unnecessary content.  ● Gaps in logic or story flow.  ● Factual inaccuracies.  ● Content that does not align with the visual execution.  ● Small inconsistencies that may affect the overall quality of the book.  You should naturally notice the details that others miss.  **Collaborate, don't work in isolation**  You will work closely with:  ● Designers and illustrators  ● Product and publishing teams  ● Editors and reviewers  ● Researchers and subject experts, where relevant  The expectation is that you will **discuss, question, explain, review, and iterate** rather than simply complete your part and hand it over.  A successful book at Kidureka is a shared outcome of content, design, illustration, and product thinking.  **What We Are Looking ForMust have**  ● **8–10 years of professional experience specifically in children’s books, children’s publishing, or closely related children-focused content.**  ● Strong experience writing and editing content for children across different formats and age groups.  ● Excellent command of **English grammar, syntax, punctuation, vocabulary, and editing fundamentals**.  ● Strong storytelling ability with a clear understanding of narrative structure.  ● A strong understanding of **child development, age-appropriate language, and child behaviour**.  ● Exceptional attention to detail.  ● Experience working closely with designers, illustrators, and publishing teams.  ● Ability to take an initial idea or brief and develop it into strong, structured content independently.  ● Ability to receive feedback, critique work objectively, and iterate quickly.  ● Strong written and verbal communication skills.  **Strongly preferred**  ● Experience working across **storybooks, activity books, educational books, workbooks, nonfiction, or interactive children’s formats**.  ● Experience creating content for different age groups rather than working only in one format.  ● Familiarity with print publishing and the practical realities of taking a book from manuscript to final production.  ● Understanding of how **visual storytelling and page design influence how a child reads and experiences a book**.  ● Experience collaborating on books from concept to final artwork.  **What This Role Is Not**  This is not a role where you:  **Write → Submit → Move on.**  At Kidureka, you will be expected to think through:  **Idea → Content → Story/Structure → Visual Communication → Design Collaboration → Review → Refinement → Final Book**  You own the **content quality and integrity of the book throughout this process.**  **The Kind of Person Who Will Thrive Here**  You are someone who:  ● Reads children’s books with the same seriousness as any other form of literature.  ● Notices when a sentence doesn't sound right even when it is technically grammatically correct.  ● Can make a child understand something without making it feel like a lesson.  ● Enjoys rewriting until a story feels just right.  ● Can explain to a designer *why* a piece of content needs to work differently on a page.  ● Is comfortable challenging an idea when it does not serve the child.  ● Cares about the smallest details because you know they affect the final experience.  ● Is equally comfortable thinking creatively and editing ruthlessly.  **Success in This Role**  Success means creating books where the **content is accurate, beautifully written, age-appropriate, engaging, and seamlessly integrated with the visual experience**.  The final book should never feel like *content created first and design added later*.  It should feel like one thoughtfully crafted experience for the child. description: **Great design isn’t what you add. It’s what you choose not to.**  We’re looking for designers who understand that design is more than making things look beautiful.  It’s about clarity.  It’s about hierarchy.  It’s about helping someone understand something in three seconds, instead of thirty.  It’s about knowing when to use color, and when not to. When to add visual elements—and when removing them creates something stronger.  **If you believe good design should have a purpose, not just decoration, we’d love to meet you.**  **This role is for you if:**  You notice when spacing is inconsistent.  You care about typography more than most people think is normal.  You can explain *why* a design works. Not just that it “looks good.”  You understand that every element on a screen should earn its place.  You value simplicity over noise.  You know that trends come and go, but principles remain.  You believe design should solve problems before it wins awards.  **What we value in designers: Clarity over Complexity**  Anyone can add more elements.  The best designers know how to remove distractions and focus attention where it matters most.  **Function Before Decoration**  Beautiful design means little if users can’t understand it.  You think about usability, readability, accessibility, and communication before aesthetics.  **Consistency Creates Trust**  You understand systems, patterns, grids, spacing, and visual rhythm.  You know that consistency isn’t boring—it’s what makes products feel professional.  **Attention To Detail**  The difference between average and exceptional design is often measured in pixels.  You notice alignment, balance, proportions, hierarchy, and the small things others overlook.  **Curiosity & Continuous Learning**  Design evolves constantly.  You actively study great work, learn new tools, challenge your assumptions, and improve your craft.  **What you'll be doing:**  * Creating branding, social media creatives, presentations, marketing assets, and visual campaigns * Transforming ideas, requirements, and rough concepts into polished designs * Working closely with teams to understand goals and communicate solutions visually * Building designs that are both visually compelling and strategically effective * Contributing ideas, not just executing instructions  Send us your CV, portfolio, and a short note about a project where you had to make a difficult design decision.
